cement.h1: Cement Rate in Ranchi Today (सीमेंट रेट)
cement.guideLink: Guide: how much cement a 1,000 sq ft house needs →
intro: Today's cement rate in Ranchi for ACC, Dalmia and Concreto cement, per 50 kg bag, straight from our live catalogue. Order a few bags or a full slab's worth.
cement.productsHeading: Cement brands we deliver – ACC, Dalmia, Concreto
guide: PPC and composite cement are the usual choice for brickwork, plaster and general house work. OPC 43/53 grade is used where early strength matters, such as slabs, beams and columns. Check the grade and the BIS mark printed on the bag (IS 269 for OPC, IS 1489 for PPC).

Thumb rule: a house needs about 0.4–0.45 bags of cement per sq ft of built-up area — roughly 400–450 bags for a 1,000 sq ft single floor. Our material calculator uses 0.45 bags per sq ft and adds the footings.

steel.h1: Sariya / TMT Rate in Ranchi Today (सरिया रेट)
steel.guideLink: Guide: choosing good quality TMT bars in Ranchi →
intro: Today's sariya (TMT bar) rate in Ranchi by size, per piece, straight from our live catalogue. Rungta TMT bars — a Jharkhand steel brand — in 8 mm, 10 mm, 12 mm and 16 mm for footings, columns, beams and slabs.
steel.guideHeading: Sariya rate per piece vs per kg
guide: Sariya is priced per piece (one bar). To compare with a per-kg rate, divide the piece rate by the bar's weight. Weight per metre = d² ÷ 162 kg, where d is the diameter in mm: about 0.395 kg/m for 8 mm, 0.617 kg/m for 10 mm, 0.888 kg/m for 12 mm and 1.58 kg/m for 16 mm. A standard 12 m bar therefore weighs about 4.7 kg (8 mm), 7.4 kg (10 mm), 10.7 kg (12 mm) and 19 kg (16 mm). Confirm the bar length with us before you compare.

Fe500 or Fe500D grade is the usual choice for houses; the D grade bends more before it breaks. Thumb rule: about 3.3 kg of steel per sq ft of built-up area (3.0–3.5 kg range) — roughly 3,300 kg for 1,000 sq ft. Our material calculator uses the same figure.

guide: We supply river sand (balu) only, sold per tempo load. The amount in a load depends on the vehicle, so ask us on WhatsApp for the cft in the load and compare rates per cft, not per trip.

Thumb rule: about 1.0–1.2 cft of sand per sq ft of built-up area (our calculator uses 1.1). For a quick silt check, shake some sand with water in a glass and let it settle — a thick layer of mud on top means the sand needs washing before plaster work.

gitti.rateHeading: Gitti rate per auto load today
gitti.guideHeading: Which gitti size for which work
guide: ¾-inch (20 mm) gitti is the usual size for RCC slabs, beams, columns and footings. ½-inch gitti suits thinner sections such as lintels, and PCC or flooring work.

Thumb rule: about 1.5–1.7 cft of gitti per sq ft of built-up area (our calculator uses 1.6). The amount in an auto load depends on the vehicle, so ask us on WhatsApp for the cft before you compare rates.
